claim_boundary.does_not_support: An analytic global optimum proof, specimen-calibrated onset or width, nonlinear propagation resistance, or a strict analytical HCP-to-Bai reduction.
claim_boundary.strict_hcp_to_bai_statement: The scalar Bai implementation remains an independently verified classical anchor. A strict HCP-to-Bai analytical degeneration is not closed and is not required for the finite-time same-generator discrimination claim.
claim_boundary.supports: The frozen integral implementation reproduces the propagator under its stated normal/commuting/fixed-leading-mode conditions; the HCP non-equivalence persists for three independently selected crystal orientations; and the reported selector is stable under the registered nested numerical global-search audit.

global_search.audit_boundary: This is an anchor-assisted basin-retention and convergence audit over the registered compact domain. Because the blind Sobol sample misses the narrow terminal basin, it is not a global-optimum certificate.

orientation_transfer.selection_rule: Each orientation retains its independently refined direction-wavenumber selector. The propagated gain and frozen spectral integral are reassessed on the same complete 69-state space, D-scaled Euclidean norm and identity input/output selectors; historical projected gains remain labeled diagnostics.

cases.rationale: A constant normal generator has one fixed orthonormal eigenbasis and one fixed leading mode.
The generator varies in time but remains normal, pairwise commuting, and has the same pointwise leading common eigenvector throughout the window.
Pairwise commutation alone is insufficient: when the pointwise leading common mode switches, integral(max alpha_j) exceeds max_j integral(alpha_j).

positive_controls.theorem_scope: For a pairwise-commuting normal family with a common orthonormal eigenbasis, log||Phi||_2=max_j integral Re(lambda_j)dt.  Equality with integral alpha(t)dt additionally requires one common mode to attain the pointwise maximum almost everywhere.
